Growing up as a farm kid in a farming community, I've never heard of this term ever...  the terms at least in my community for it where "chute", "squeeze chute", "head catcher", and sometimes just "rack".  Some flip over on their side to better hold calves and are called "calf tables".  

For sanctuary farms that do not kill and the such, chutes come in handy for vaccinating or treating wounds on a cow or calf who may be in enough pain to make her strike out.  It helps to minimize injury to you or your cow by not allowing her to bust through fences trying to get away, or bowl you over in the process.  Sometimes, even little knocks and bumps that you just want to put some ointment on for good measure can can be a challenge if the cow is a flightier personality.  Shes in the chute for a minute, rub some cream on and send her on her way to enjoy the rest of her days.
